purpose: A node-based editor. Visual programming is close to my rule engine interest, so I want to see how its graph is wired.

pages.title: GraphiteEditor/Graphite
pages.failed: skipped: read in the last 30 days

pages.title: maira-acosta/mintmousse-web-console
pages.reaction: A debugging dashboard dressed up as a control room, with a lot of marketing gloss over a fairly ordinary idea. Node-based editing isn't here at all, so my trip's purpose didn't land. Mildly amused by how hard the copy works to sound polished.

pages.title: littlektframework/littlekt
pages.reaction: A Kotlin WebGPU game framework, which is a long way from a node editor. The graph wiring I wanted is not here. The README is mostly install instructions and acknowledgements. Mildly useful as a reminder that libGDX-style frameworks exist, but it gave me very little for my rule engine.

pages.title: Frostfire-Interactive/Frostfire-Forge
pages.reaction: A 2D MMO engine where you build maps and spells inside the game, and it's not a node editor at all. I came for the graph wiring and found a whole Bun and WebTransport server stack with a Python translator bolted on. Nothing here about how a node graph is wired, so this gave me little for my purpose. Mildly …

pages.title: renzora/engine
pages.reaction: A big Rust game engine with a visual editor, but the node graph I came for is only hinted at: material nodes that generate WESL, not a general graph wiring I can read. Lots of features, very little about how the graph actually connects. Mildly useful, mostly a wall of checkmarks.
